user_requirements: This is a CLIENT-READINESS REVIEW of REPORT.md — ASG Security's LCF Pilot Accountability & Value Report, about to be sent to the client (Heart of the City / Edward Caughey) and forwarded to Auckland Council funding administrators. The numbers have already been independently verified in a prior review and must NOT be changed. Your sole job is disclosure hygiene and client-facing polish: (1) sweep the entire report line by line against internal_sensitivity_brief.txt and flag ANY leakage of internal ASG operational matters — staffing failures, equipment/admin failures, internal reporting-quality mechanics beyond the approved neutral provenance statement, internal management matters, named staff, or identifiable other ASG clients/sites; (2) flag anything that blames or embarrasses a precinct business, Police, or Council; (3) assess whether each of the report's sections reads professionally for a client/funder audience — flag awkward phrasing, anything defensive, and anything that invites a question ASG would rather answer in person; (4) check the §13 data-sources paragraph specifically: it must keep an honest compilation-method statement but should not over-disclose internal reporting mechanics — propose tightened wording if needed. Output a findings list with severity (BLOCKER / RECOMMENDED / OPTIONAL), quoting the exact current text and giving exact replacement text for each. If the report is clean, say so explicitly per category. Do not rewrite the report; produce the findings list only.
acquirer_context: ASG Security is the supplier; Heart of the City is the client and funding holder; Auckland Council administers the Local Crime Fund. The report is a contractual accountability deliverable. ASG's CEO has approved the three capacity instances in section 4 for inclusion. The commercial relationship is ongoing and ASG is positioning for an extended engagement, so the report must be honest but must not air internal operational problems.
